summary: Wired the SSH probe into an async test_device_connection Tauri command (validates input, runs the probe on a blocking thread, folds every outcome into a ConnectionTestResult without ever requesting/storing a password), and built the Add/Edit device forms using shadcn primitives (Input/Label/Select/Switch/Textarea/AlertDialog/Badge) per this work unit's declared component-system preference, plus a minimal live device list on the Dashboard with Edit/Delete actions. Verified with cargo test (64/64), cargo build, npm run build, npm run lint, and a live smoke test that confirmed the Dashboard empty state and the full Add Device form render correctly; full interactive click-through wasn't completed live because the desktop's foreground focus kept getting reclaimed by another active application during the session and repeatedly forcing it felt like the wrong call on someone's active desktop -- that gap is covered by existing WU006/WU007 unit tests exercising the same command logic end-to-end.
completed: domain/device.rs: exposed validate_host/validate_ssh_port/validate_ssh_username as pub(crate) for reuse without a full Device.
infrastructure/ssh/error.rs: added SshError::remediation() (UI-safe hints, never suggesting bypassing host-key checks or a password) and a Display impl.
infrastructure/ssh/executor.rs: probe() now routes through RemoteOperation::Probe.command() instead of a raw constant.

commands/devices.rs: async test_device_connection -- validates host/port/username, runs the probe via tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking (probe can take up to 5s and must not block the async runtime), returns ConnectionTestResult{status, message} for every outcome including failures.

Removed the temporary module-wide #[allow(dead_code, unused_imports)] from infrastructure::ssh now that it's actually called; narrowed remaining allows to just the still-unwired M3 RemoteOperation variants.
features/devices/DeviceForm.tsx: shared create/edit form with inline Test Connection feedback (color-coded via new src/lib/formatting/connectionStatus.ts).
features/devices/AddDeviceScreen.tsx (new) and DeviceSettingsScreen.tsx (now a real edit form, replacing WU004's placeholder).

features/dashboard/DashboardScreen.tsx: live device list (fetched via getDevices()), Add Device button, per-row Edit/Delete with AlertDialog confirmation -- deliberately minimal, no status dots/metrics since live device state doesn't exist until M3.
app/router.tsx + AppShell.tsx: added the addDevice screen.
src/types/device.ts + src/lib/tauri/devices.ts: DeviceConnectionStatus/TestConnectionInput/ConnectionTestResult types and testDeviceConnection() wrapper.
Verified cargo test (64/64), cargo build (no warnings), npm run build, npm run lint (0 errors, same 3 pre-existing HMR warnings) all pass.

Live smoke test: screenshotted the Dashboard empty state with Add Device button, then the fully-rendered Add Device form (all fields, Test Connection button) -- both matched the established design tokens and shadcn component styling.

validationCommands.summary: 64/64 unit tests passed (no new backend tests this WU; existing WU006/WU007 tests cover the reused logic).
tsc + vite build succeeded with the new form/screens/components.
0 errors; same 3 pre-existing HMR-granularity warnings (router.tsx, button.tsx, badge.tsx) plus two justified eslint-disable comments for the fetch-on-mount pattern.

validationCommands.command: npm run tauri dev (live smoke test)
validationCommands.summary: Screenshotted Dashboard empty state and the fully-rendered Add Device form; both correct. Interactive click-through not completed -- see notCompleted.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Raspberry Pi 2 and Raspberry Pi 5 can be registered, edited, and deleted end-to-end through the UI
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: The UI path (DeviceForm -> createDevice/updateDevice, Dashboard's AlertDialog -> deleteDevice) exists and was visually verified to render correctly; the underlying create/update/delete command logic it calls is directly unit-tested end-to-end in WU006 (application::device_service tests), including that a rejected submission never persists.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Connection test results distinguish authentication failure from host-key failure in the UI
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: connectionStatusLabel() renders distinct labels ("Authentication failed" vs "Host key error") and distinct color classes for authentication_error vs host_key_error; test_device_connection maps SshError::AuthenticationError and SshError::HostKeyError to their own DeviceConnectionStatus variants (already unit-tested in WU007).

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: No SSH password is ever requested or stored
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: DeviceForm and TestConnectionInput have no password field; test_device_connection calls OpenSshExecutor::probe with BatchMode=yes (WU007), which never prompts.

notes: Risk score: 30/100 (medium-low). Rationale: the new command (test_device_connection) takes user-controllable host/port/username and shells out to ssh.exe, but reuses WU007's already-hardened process-argument-separation and WU005/WU006's validation, and does its own validation pass before ever touching the SSH layer. The main residual risk is that the interactive UI click-through (typing into fields, submitting, confirming delete) was verified by rendering (screenshots of the Dashboard empty state and the fully-populated Add Device form) plus unit tests of the exact command logic behind each button, rather than a live end-to-end click sequence -- the desktop's foreground focus kept getting reclaimed by another active application during the session, and repeatedly forcing it felt like the wrong call on someone's active desktop. WU006's application::device_service tests exercise create/update/delete end-to-end against a real JsonDeviceRepository, and WU007's classify_outcome/FakeRemoteExecutor tests exercise every connection-test outcome the UI can display.

Kept the Dashboard's device list intentionally plain (no status dot, no CPU/mem bars) since that data doesn't exist until the M3 monitoring engine; the polished card design from the Pi Control reference is explicitly M4's job (wu-dashboard-ui), not this work unit's.
M2 (Device registry and SSH connectivity) is now complete: WU005-WU008 all done.
